System Bus Access Control and Status

Absolute Address:
Base Offset:

Source:

Description

Controls and status for the System Bus Access master. Writes while sbbusy=1 result in undefined behavior.

Field Descriptions

sbversion

System Bus interface version. 0=pre-2018 drafts, 1=this version (0.13).

_reserved_28_23

Reserved.

sbbusyerror

System bus busy error. Set if access attempted while busy or read while read in progress. No new access if set.

sbbusy

1: System bus master is busy. Goes high on access request, low on completion.

sbreadonaddr

1: Every write to sbaddress0 automatically triggers a system bus read at the new address.

sbaccess

Access size for system bus accesses: 0=8-bit, 1=16-bit, 2=32-bit, 3=64-bit, 4=128-bit. If unsupported, access fails, sberror=4.

sbautoincrement

1: sbaddress is incremented by access size (from sbaccess) after every system bus access.

sbreadondata

1: Every read from sbdata0 automatically triggers a system bus read at (possibly auto-incremented) address.

_reserved_14_12

Reserved.

sberror

System bus master error flags. No new access if non-zero. 0=none, 1=timeout, 2=bad_address, 3=alignment, 4=unsupported_size, 7=other.

sbasize

Width of system bus addresses in bits (e.g., 32 for 32-bit addresses). 0 indicates no bus access support. NOTE: This field is 4 bits wide ([8:5]), which is insufficient to directly store typical bus widths like 32 or 64. This implies the value is an encoding or there is a spec issue. The text implies it stores values like 32, 64, etc (e.g. 'if sbasize < 33').

sbaccess128

1: 128-bit system bus accesses are supported.

sbaccess64

1: 64-bit system bus accesses are supported.

sbaccess32

1: 32-bit system bus accesses are supported.

sbaccess16

1: 16-bit system bus accesses are supported.

sbaccess8

1: 8-bit system bus accesses are supported.
